info.name: IRoute — Driver Job Flow
info.description:
Complete driver mobile job flow from login to job closed.
Follows A1 through A10 as defined in IRoute document.
Use {{base_url}} variable = http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/mobile
Use {{access_token}} variable = filled automatically after login.
Use {{job_id}} variable = filled after dashboard call.
Use {{shipment_id}} variable = filled after A4 executes.
Use {{capture_bundle_id}} variable = filled after POD capture.

request.description:
STEP 1 — FIRST API TO CALL.
Send driver phone, password, tenant_id in body.
After success, access_token is auto-saved to collection variable.
All subsequent requests use Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}.
Response key is data.access_token (not 'access', not 'token').
If login fails check: phone format, password, tenant_id is correct.

exec: pm.test("Login successful, token saved", function() { pm.expect(resp.status).to.eql(1); });
pm.test("Login failed — check phone, password, tenant_id", function() { pm.expect(resp.status).to.eql(1); });

request.description:
STEP 2 — CALL AFTER LOGIN.
Returns active job assigned to driver.
job_id and job_type are auto-saved from response.
job_type will be 'shipment' for normal delivery jobs.
If no active_job in response then no job is assigned yet.
Check data.active_job.job_id and data.active_job.job_type.
These variables are used in all job detail and action calls.

exec: pm.test("Active job found, job_id saved", function() { pm.expect(resp.data.active_job.job_id).to.exist; });
pm.test("No active job assigned to driver", function() { pm.expect(resp.data.active_job).to.exist; });

request.description:
STEP 3 — CALL TO SEE FULL JOB STATE BEFORE ANY ACTION.
URL uses job_type and job_id from dashboard response.
job_type is usually 'shipment'.
Response shows current state, next allowed action, cargo, addresses.
Check data.next_action to know which action to fire next.
Check data.shipment_id — will be null until A4 fires.
This API can be called anytime to refresh job state.

STEP 4 — FIRST DRIVER ACTION IN THE JOB.
action_code A1 is in the URL path, not in the body.
client_action_id must be unique per firing — use a UUID.
content_hash is required — use any UUID for testing.
latitude and longitude are GPS coordinates.
After A1 fires: Booking Execution Date is stamped.
Booking Item status moves to In Execution.
Next action to fire is A2 Pickup Arrival.

STEP 5 — DRIVER ARRIVED AT PICKUP LOCATION.
Audit only action — captures GPS and timestamp.
Does not change Shipment or Booking status.
Just records that driver reached the loading address.
Next action to fire is A3 Start Loading.

STEP 6 — LOADING HAS STARTED.
Audit only action — captures GPS and timestamp.
Does not change Shipment or Booking status.
PREREQUISITE FOR A4 — A3 must fire before A4 can fire.
Next action is A4 Confirm Loaded which is the POINT OF NO RETURN.

item.name: 07 — Execute A4 — Confirm Loaded (POINT OF NO RETURN)

request.description:
STEP 7 — MOST IMPORTANT ACTION. POINT OF NO RETURN.
After this fires THREE things are atomically created:
  1. Shipment record (status = Loaded)
  2. Truck Movement Log record (status = Scheduled)
  3. Booking Item status advances to In Execution
All three succeed together or none succeed.
If app crashes mid-action nothing is created — safe to retry.
AFTER THIS ACTION: job cannot be cancelled normally.
shipment_id is auto-saved from response for use in later APIs.
Media is REQUIRED — photos of loaded cargo.
At least 2 photos should be sent.
Next action is A5 Depart In Transit.

STEP 8 — TRUCK HAS DEPARTED.
Advances EXISTING records — does NOT create new ones.
Shipment status changes: Loaded → In Transit
Truck Movement Log status changes: Scheduled → In Progress
Start Time is stamped on Movement Log.
GPS at departure point is captured.
Next action is A6 Delivery Arrival.

STEP 9 — DRIVER ARRIVED AT DELIVERY LOCATION.
Shipment status changes: In Transit → At Delivery
GPS at delivery point is captured.
After this delivery address can no longer be changed.
Next step is POD Capture (separate API) then A7 Upload POD.

body.raw:
{
  "client_capture_id": "pod-cap-{{$guid}}",
  "content_hash": "{{$guid}}",
  "workflow_version": "1.0",
  "pod_type": "soft_copy",
  "target_action_code": "A7",
  "latitude": 21.3891,
  "longitude": 39.8579,
  "notes": "Delivery note signed by receiver",
  "media": [
    {
      "media_type": "photo",
      "file_ref": "signed_delivery_note_page1.jpg",
      "file_name": "delivery_note_p1.jpg",
      "description": "Page 1 of signed delivery note",
      "sort_order": 1
    }
  ]
}

request.description:
STEP 10 — STAGE POD EVIDENCE BEFORE FIRING A7.
This is a STAGING API — does NOT create the POD Record yet.
Does NOT change Shipment status.
Does NOT write to Action Log.
It only stages Layer 1 (Digital GPS/photos) and Layer 2 (Soft Copy scans).
Uses shipment_id variable saved from A4 response.
capture_bundle_id is auto-saved for use in A7 execute call.
MUST call this before A7.
Then pass capture_bundle_id to the A7 execute request body.

exec: pm.test("POD bundle staged, capture_bundle_id saved", function() { pm.expect(resp.data.capture_bundle_id).to.exist; });

item.name: 11 — Execute A7 — Upload POD (Creates POD Record)

request.description:
STEP 11 — UPLOAD POD AND CREATE POD RECORD.
REQUIRES capture_bundle_id from Step 10 POD Capture call.
Pass capture_bundle_id in the body (also accepted as bundle_id or pod_capture_bundle_id).
When A7 fires it atomically:
  1. Creates the POD Record (POD-YYYY-NNNN)
  2. Advances Shipment status: At Delivery → POD Submitted
  3. Writes Action Log entry
Layer 1 = Digital Evidence (GPS, photos already staged in bundle)
Layer 2 = Soft Copy (scanned delivery note already staged in bundle)
Layer 3 = Hard Copy handled separately by Ops on desktop — NOT here.
After A7: Ops must verify POD before Shipment can advance.
For COD orders: A9 Collect Payment fires after A7.
For Credit orders: A8 Unloading Completed fires after A7.

STEP 12 — UNLOADING IS DONE.
Truck Movement Log status changes: In Progress → Completed
End Time is stamped on Movement Log.
Asset-side leg is now CLOSED at this point.
Shipment commercial side stays open until A10.
For COD orders: fire A9 Collect Payment before or after A8.
For Credit orders: A8 leads directly to A10 Job Closed
(after POD is verified by Ops).

item.name: 13 — Payment Collection — A9 COD Only (Collect Cash)

request.description:
STEP 13 — COD CASH COLLECTION (ONLY FOR COD ORDER TYPE).
SKIP THIS STEP FOR CREDIT ORDERS.
This calls Payment Collection API which internally fires A9.
Uses shipment_id variable saved from A4.
amount = actual cash collected from customer.
If amount differs from expected COD Amount:
  - Driver is NOT blocked.
  - Variance is FLAGGED for Ops follow-up.
  - Treasury Transaction is still created with actual amount.
  - Shipment COD Payment Status = Collected regardless.
After this fires:
  - Driver Treasury Transaction created (Debit, Client Pay)
  - Driver wallet balance increases by collected amount
  - Ops will initiate Internal Transfer to collection wallet later
Next action is A10 Job Closed (after POD verified by Ops).

STEP 14 — FINAL ACTION. CLOSES THE JOB.
PREREQUISITES THAT MUST BE MET BEFORE A10 CAN FIRE:
  - A8 Unloading Completed must have fired
  - POD must be Compliant (verified by Ops)
  - For COD: COD Payment Status must be Collected (A9 fired)
When A10 fires:
  - Shipment status: Delivered → Closed (TERMINAL)
  - Booking Item status: In Execution → Executed
  - Booking derived status recomputes to Executed
After A10: Driver returns to Home in On Call mode.
After A10: Shipment becomes eligible for SIR billing sweep.
Nothing can reverse this action.

OPTIONAL — CAN BE CALLED AT ANY POINT DURING THE JOB.
issue_type values: delay, vehicle_breakdown, customer_unavailable,
  payment_dispute, pod_issue, accident, route_blocked, other
severity values: low, medium, high, critical
This does NOT stop the job flow.
Issue is sent to Ops supervisor for acknowledgement.
Driver continues normal action flow alongside.
